title: Fit each quadcopter motor with a propeller whose leading edges lead the way it turns
instruction: Fit a propeller on each of the drone's four motors, standing upright and centred on the motor's top (hub up, as they lie on the mats). The red arrow beside each motor shows which way that motor turns: use a propeller whose leading edges, the raised white strips along one side of each blade, lead in that direction. Two of the six propellers are spares.
context: Drone and robotics technicians fit propellers on every build and repair (O*NET 17-3024.01 Robotics Technicians). On a quadcopter neighbouring motors turn opposite ways, so two motors take clockwise (CW) propellers and two counter-clockwise (CCW) ones, and a propeller's hand is read from its blades: the leading edge, the higher and thicker edge of each pitched blade, must lead in the motor's direction of turn. No turn makes a CW propeller into a CCW one, so the right part must be chosen for each motor. A propeller of the wrong hand, or one fitted upside down, pushes air the wrong way and the drone flips over at take-off; it is a classic first-build error, and technicians check the hands at every propeller change. Here each mat also holds a spare of the hand that the other side's rear motor must not have.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Everything is fixed except the six propellers. (1) Quadcopter frame without propellers, standing in for a 5-inch quad with its front toward +x: four black carbon-fibre arms, flat bars 16 mm wide and 8 mm thick lying on the table along the diagonals from 20 mm to 142 mm out from the frame's centre at x 30.0 cm, y 0, and a black carbon-fibre centre plate 70 x 70 x 12 mm centred on them (resting on the arms, its top 20 mm up). (2) Four motors: dark grey anodised aluminium cylinders 28 mm across and 30 mm tall standing on the arms' ends, top face 38 mm above the table, axes at front left (FL) x 38.0, y +10.0 cm; front right (FR) x 38.0, y -10.0 cm; rear left (RL) x 22.0, y +10.0 cm; rear right (RR) x 22.0, y -10.0 cm. (3) Four rotation arrows of red plastic strip 5 mm wide and 1 mm thick on the table, layered where strips cross (at most 4 mm high), one round the outer side of each motor: an arc of radius 32 mm (to the strip's centre line) about the motor's axis, spanning 100 degrees centred on the arm's outward line, made of three straight strips, with a head of two 12 mm strips at its leading end, each swept back 40 degrees. The FL and RR arrows point clockwise seen from above, FR and RL counter-clockwise (an X quad: diagonal motors turn the same way). (4) Two light grey foam mats 140 x 180 x 3 mm (140 mm along x), centred at x 20.0 cm, y +28.5 and -28.5 cm. (5) Six loose propellers, 20 g each, each one rigid glass-filled nylon part: a grey hub, a cylinder 22 mm across and 34 mm tall; two black blades 55 x 18 x 4 mm on opposite sides at the hub's foot, from 8 to 63 mm out from its axis (126 mm tip to tip); on top of each blade a raised white leading-edge strip 52 x 6 x 3 mm along one long side, flush with that side, from the hub to the tip. Hand: seen from above with the blades along x, a clockwise (CW) propeller has its strips on the -y side of the +x blade and the +y side of the -x blade (the edges that lead when it turns clockwise); a counter-clockwise (CCW) one is its mirror image. All six lie hub up on the mats, blades along x, hubs at x 20.0 cm: left mat y +23.0 CW, +28.5 CCW, +34.0 CCW; right mat y -23.0 CCW, -28.5 CW, -34.0 CW. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored on the end state: the trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 2.5 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. A propeller 'stands on' a motor when its hub's axis is within 8 degrees of vertical, the centre of the hub's bottom face is within 6 mm of the motor's axis seen from above, and that face is within 3 mm of the motor's top (above or below). It stands on the motor 'upside down' when its hub's top face meets the same 6 mm and 3 mm with its axis within 8 degrees of vertical (blades uppermost). A propeller tilted more than 8 degrees, off-centre by more than 6 mm, resting on another propeller, lying on the frame or on a mat, held higher or off the table stands on no motor. A propeller's hand is fixed by its shape (no turn about the vertical changes it; see setup) and is read from its white strips. Each motor's hand is the way its red arrow points: FL and RR clockwise (CW), FR and RL counter-clockwise (CCW). A motor is 'fitted' when a propeller of its own hand stands upright on it and is at rest: the centres of its hub's bottom and top faces and both blade tips each stayed within 2 mm of where they are now over the last 0.5 s. Score 0 if any propeller of the wrong hand stands on a motor, or any propeller stands on a motor upside down, at rest or not: that drone flips at take-off. Otherwise 0.25 for each fitted motor. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 (for example: nothing fitted 0; FL fitted with a CW propeller 0.25; both left motors fitted 0.5; three fitted and RR empty 0.75; all four fitted 1.0; three fitted and a CCW propeller on RR 0; three fitted and the fourth motor's propeller upside down on it 0). Any propeller of the right hand counts, from either mat; spares may stay on the mats or go anywhere off the motors. Only the propellers' poses are read, whether or not a gripper still holds one. In a real trial a top photo shows which propeller stands on which motor and on which side of each blade its white strip lies, and a rule held across the motor's top gives the centring.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction. Propellers do not spin; the motors are unpowered fixed cylinders with no shaft or nut, so 'fitted' means standing centred on the motor's top. The hub is 34 mm tall (real about 7 mm) so a gripper can hold it above the blades, a propeller weighs 20 g (real 4-5 g), and blade pitch is shown by a raised strip on each leading edge. The arrows lie on the table beside the motors (a real frame prints them on the arms). Only the propellers' poses are scored.
reset_notes: Lay the six propellers back hub up on the mats, blades along x, hubs at x 20.0 cm: left mat y +23.0 CW, +28.5 CCW, +34.0 CCW; right mat y -23.0 CCW, -28.5 CW, -34.0 CW (a CW propeller has the strip of its +x blade on the -y side). Nothing is consumed; the frame, motors, arrows and mats are fixed.
